case_name: United States of America Ex Rel. Ciro M. Caruso, N. J. S. P. No. 56349 v. United States Board of Parole

headnotes.text: A habeas petitioner's failure to take an administrative appeal from a parole authority's decision to leave a violator warrant unexecuted as a detainer does not require dismissal for non-exhaustion where the agency no longer treats such decisions as subject to administrative appellate review, since requiring exhaustion would be meaningless.

headnotes.text: A federal parolee imprisoned for a new crime committed on parole has no liberty interest in a prompt revocation hearing on an unexecuted violator warrant; loss of liberty begins only when the warrant is executed. That the intervening sentence is a state rather than federal sentence makes no difference to the effect on the federal sentence.

headnotes.text: A state prisoner is not entitled to an immediate federal revocation hearing when an unexecuted federal parole violator warrant based on a state felony committed on parole is lodged as a detainer. Claimed loss of access to state prison programs and early state parole is too speculative to be a liberty deprivation and, if anything, is attributable to state officials.
